_comment: Claude-built, hand-labelled set (n=20). Expected entries were chosen by reading the inventory and grepping raw text, not by running search_profile. Names only; no inventory text. An entry is expected when it provides direct evidence for the query, not for a passing mention.

queries.query: Redis caching layer to reduce API latency
queries.justification: The only entry that implements a caching layer on Redis; the other Redis entries use it as a job-queue backend or infrastructure, which a caching requirement does not ask for.

queries.query: RAG pipeline with vector database and embeddings
queries.justification: Both internships build retrieval-augmented pipelines over a vector store (pgvector at one, ChromaDB with sentence-transformers at the other) and report retrieval evaluation.
Only entry that uses Spring Boot (and Java) in both its technology list and its achievements.

Three entries ship WebSocket-based realtime behaviour (STOMP notifications, queue progress transport, Socket.io messaging). Entries that only use server-sent events are excluded because the query names WebSocket.
The CUDA project is the direct evidence; the NVIDIA deep-learning certification validates GPU-accelerated training skills.
A LangGraph agentic platform, an eight-agent LLM pipeline, and a subagent-orchestrated Claude Code setup are the three entries that build multi-agent systems.

queries.query: .NET Core C# backend with Entity Framework
queries.justification: The two backends built on .NET and Entity Framework Core. The desktop audio app also uses C# but is not a backend.

queries.query: CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI
queries.justification: Entries whose technology lists and achievements include GitLab CI/CD or GitHub Actions workflows.

queries.query: NestJS REST API with PostgreSQL and Prisma
queries.justification: Four entries combine NestJS with PostgreSQL and Prisma in their technology lists.
The only entry that lists and describes Zustand; other React entries do not mention it.
BullMQ workers in two projects, and RQ-on-Redis worker queues in the pipeline suite and the AI internship.
Entries that automate a real browser (Playwright or its patchright fork) or build scrapers as a core feature.

queries.query: Supabase Postgres row level security authentication
queries.justification: Entries built on Supabase with RLS or Supabase auth/realtime described in the achievements.
Both generate voice-over audio with TTS engines as part of a pipeline.
The only entry that trains and evaluates text classifiers with scikit-learn and BERT.

queries.query: Model Context Protocol MCP server tools
queries.justification: Two MCP certifications plus the project that runs an MCP server in a daily Claude Code setup.
AnyDeck is an Expo and React Native app; the freelance entry lists Expo (React Native) for a prototype. Hybrid Capacitor and native Kotlin work is excluded because the query names React Native.
The two projects that ship Electron desktop apps.
The two internships that build Angular front ends.

expected.name: Get the Most Out of Jira
Apply Agile Practices to Manage Your Work
Configure Agile Boards for Jira Spaces

queries.justification: Five certifications whose names cover Scrum, Agile practice and Jira. Experience entries that mention agile delivery in passing are not counted.
